it said the object is always what belongs to God; Psa 104:34 names no object of the meditation

actions.new_text: Devout meditation on God, his law and his works: the person murmurs over and dwells on the law, God's deeds or God himself, by day and night, on the bed and in the watches of the night, and the law is called his meditation. In Job 15:4 meditation before God is what is hindered, and in Psa 104:34 the psalmist asks that his meditation be pleasing to God. Where an object is named it belongs to God, and the setting is private and continual. Verses: Jos 1:8, Psa 63:6, Psa 77:12, Psa 119:15, Psa 119:23, Psa 119:27, Psa 119:48, Psa 119:78, Psa 119:148, Psa 143:5, Psa 145:5, Psa 1:2, Job 15:4, Psa 104:34, Psa 119:97, Psa 119:99.
actions.checked: Psa 104:34 (May my meditation be pleasing to him: no object named) against the other verses of the sense
actions.reason: evidence validation (B5): it said the object is always what belongs to God; Psa 104:34 names no object of the meditation

actions.new_text: Pondering as turning a matter over in the mind: Mary treasures up the things told and ponders them in her heart, Peter ponders the vision as the Spirit speaks, and in Pro 15:28 the righteous man's heart weighs a reply before his mouth speaks. In each the thought is held inwardly; in Pro 15:28 it comes before the speaking. Verses: Luk 2:19, Act 10:19, Pro 15:28.
actions.checked: Luk 2:19 (nothing follows the pondering in the verse), Act 10:19, Pro 15:28
actions.reason: evidence validation (B5): it said in each verse the thought precedes what follows; in Luk 2:19 nothing follows it in the verse
